methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective study on 103 (99 after small-nodule exclusion) DCE-MRI cases, comparing seven SAM/MedSAM variants under a 5-fold cross-validation scheme with consistent preprocessing, optimizer, and training settings across all models. Strengths: factorial design (initial weights x mask strategy x prompt box type), baseline comparisons with U-Net and UNETR, fixed hyperparameters, and code/model release on GitHub. Limitations: small single-center dataset, benign/malignant imbalance (23 vs 80), no external validation, the fixed prompt box is derived from ground-truth slice with maximum nodule area (still requires annotation at test time, somewhat circular), and the 'fully automated' framing is inconsistent with reliance on GT-derived fixed boxes. Paired t-test reported as main test for Dice/HD95 which may not fully address the 5-fold dependency structure; Nemenyi post-hoc used.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Breast MRI segmentation is clinically relevant for lesion characterization, but the study provides a technical comparison without patient-level outcomes or clinical workflow integration. Reported Dice of about 80.90% is comparable to existing methods but not demonstrated to improve diagnostic or treatment decisions. LoE 5 (basic/technical science).

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe data collection, preprocessing, model variants, training configuration, and evaluation metrics in adequate detail. Code, trained models, and preprocessing scripts are released via a GitHub link, which supports reproducibility. However, the patient cohort dataset itself is not made publicly available (local IRB), benign/malignant imbalance is noted but not addressed in training, and the Results section has several grammatical issues and unclear sentences (e.g., 'MedSAM-nm segmentation results were the best, MedSAM-nm results were the second-best' which appears to be a typo).

novelty_literature.justification: SAM and MedSAM applied to medical images is a very active area with multiple published adaptations already in breast ultrasound (refs 30-32), various SAM-medical variants (refs 26-29), and prior SAM-UNet/SAM-Med2.5D architectures (ref 33). The modest novelty here is specifically applying SAM variants to breast DCE-MRI (which the authors explicitly identify as under-studied relative to ultrasound) and systematically comparing initial weights, mask usage, and prompt types. Incremental methodological comparison rather than a new framework.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript has significant presentation issues: grammatical errors throughout ('the training segmentation models for medical images is still challenging', 'the feature maps is decoded'), an evident typo in Results ('MedSAM-nm segmentation results were the best, MedSAM-nm results were the second-best' — one should be a different variant), inconsistent terminology (organ mask vs breast mask vs mammary mask), and unclear sentences about the fixed prompt box construction. The figure captions describe method flows but key experimental codes in Table 1 are not defined within the text.

key_strengths: Systematic factorial comparison of seven SAM/MedSAM configurations under a consistent 5-fold cross-validation protocol
Explicit baseline comparison with U-Net and UNETR under identical training settings
Code, trained models, and preprocessing scripts released via GitHub
Clear demonstration that MedSAM initialization outperforms SAM, and that hard-mask multiplication with breast mask is detrimental
Focus on DCE-MRI, an under-studied modality for SAM compared with ultrasound
key_concerns: Single-center 103-case dataset with benign/malignant imbalance (23 vs 80) and no external validation
Fixed prompt box is derived from ground-truth nodule bounding box on the maximum-area slice, contradicting claims of practical applicability
Multiple typographical errors including 'MedSAM-nm was the best, MedSAM-nm was second-best' in Results, suggesting inadequate proofreading
Grammatical issues pervasive throughout the manuscript, impeding clear interpretation
No ablation of hyperparameters or learning rate; limited statistical treatment of cross-validation fold dependence
Novelty limited: SAM/MedSAM medical adaptation is heavily published territory
chief_reviewer.rationale: A technically reasonable but pedestrian SAM-for-medical-images comparison on a small single-center breast MRI dataset, limited by small n, circular prompt box construction, multiple proofreading errors, and incremental novelty — Tier 4 with major revisions.
